_synthetic: SYNTHETIC COVERAGE SAMPLE. Blank government form, invented taxpayer. Every value is an obvious placeholder (Testcorp, 000-00-0000, 555-01xx). No real PII. Its job is to exercise every MAPPED path in 433a.map.json sections 1-3, the whole of section 4, and the section 5 income/expense grid - it is not a realistic return.
_coverage_notes: SECTION 5 (map v5). All 31 grid values are DISTINCT across both panels - not merely distinct within a panel. On sheet 6 every internal field-name suffix lags its printed line by one, so a one-row shift would land plausible money in the wrong printed category; only a grid with no repeated figure makes that shift visible in the read-back.

The totals are real arithmetic on the rows above them, so they cross-check the rows: 35_total_income 12545 = the fourteen income amounts (5210+3120+145+880+615+430+275+190+355+240+505+320+165+95), 50_total_living_expenses 12477 = the fourteen expense amounts (3210+2450+735+512+130+620+645+410+815+175+1190+960+285+340), and 51_net_difference 68 = 12545 - 12477. A row that printed one line off would break at least one of those sums.

Both write-in rows (printed 33 and 34) carry a DESCRIPTION and an amount. The description cells are the only text in an otherwise all-money grid, so if a description ever landed in a money column it would be obvious rather than plausible.

allowable_household_size is DELIBERATELY ABSENT (map v6), so the fill exercises the derivation path rather than the override: taxpayer 1 + spouse 1 + the 4 slotted members with claimed_on_1040=yes = 6. That is the IRS National Standards default, which counts persons allowed as dependents on the most recent return, not occupants of the home. 6 is still above the published 1-4 range, so the per-additional-person arithmetic is exercised rather than skipped. The earlier household_size of 7 was the raw headcount and was the wrong basis; it priced line 36 at 3367 where the IRS default gives 2970.

allowable_under_65_count 5 + allowable_65_over_count 1 replace the single age_band input (map v6). 433-A prints ONE out-of-pocket line for a household that can span both bands, so a single band could not express this sample: 'Sample Household Four' is 71 and belongs in the 65-over band, and the old age_band of 'under_65' priced all seven people at the under-65 rate. The two counts sum to 6, which is the derived household above - that sum is a HARD STOP if it disagrees, because the two allowable cells would otherwise be priced on two different households.

Keyed against map_version 6. Key prefixes follow PRINTED line numbers, not internal field names: the lawsuit block is 7_* (its widgets are named _6) and bankruptcy is 8_* (named _7). Renaming here tracks the map rename.

3c_business_type is 'llc' AND 3c_business_type_other_desc carries text. On a real form those contradict (the Other description belongs with the Other box). Both are present here deliberately so the ListOther target is proven to write; it is coverage, not a modelling claim.
Pay periods differ on purpose - taxpayer bi-weekly, spouse monthly - so a copy/paste error between the 4h and 5h blocks shows up in the read-back instead of hiding behind identical values.
Option values deliberately vary in case and padding (' Yes ', 'YES', booleans) to exercise the trim + case-insensitive match.
household_members carries SIX records against five slots: the sixth exists to prove overflow is logged and dropped rather than thrown or silently written.
1a_full_name is 42 chars because that cell carries /MaxLen 45. Longer input is refused by the field, and the fill stops rather than blanking it.

The six split inputs are written in FOUR DIFFERENT human formats on purpose - parenthesised, dashed, bare digits, dotted, and an EIN both with and without its hyphen. All six must strip to the same digits and land in the same halves; if `strip` regressed, only some of them would break, which is the point.
Tenure and dependent-count cells are tiny (/MaxLen 2 and 10) and the two lived-abroad dates are /MaxLen 8, so values here are sized to the printed cell, not to prose.

SECTION 4. bank_accounts carries FIVE records against four slots - the fifth proves overflow is logged and dropped on a text-only group, the same way household_members proves it on a group with checkboxes. The four Section 4 groups have no checkboxes at all, which is what exercises the optional-`checkboxes` path in the group handler.

13e_total_cash (20600) is deliberately the arithmetic sum of 12_total_cash_on_hand (1500) and the four SLOTTED account balances (4100+6200+3300+5500). The dropped fifth account's 9900 is excluded on purpose: if overflow ever silently wrote into a slot, the printed total would stop agreeing with the printed rows and the read-back would show it.

13_accounts_balance_as_of and 14_investments_loan_balance_as_of are the column-header 'As of' DATE cells (/MaxLen 8, mmddyyyy) - not money. The per-row balance cells beneath them are /MaxLen 12 money. Both carry the same bled 'mmddyyyy' caption, so the two are only distinguishable by cell size, and that is exactly the confusion these values are sized to catch.

real_property descriptions are distinct per row ('Row 18a' / 'Row 18b' / 'Row 18c') and vehicles differ in year, make/model AND mileage (11111 / 22222 / 33333). The map's row indices are INVERTED against print order on both tables, so identical filler would have hidden a swapped row; distinct values make a swap visible in one glance at the read-back grid.

Vehicle make_model writes to a target named ...18aMILE and mileage writes to one named ...MKMDL. That inversion is in the form, not in this sample: the printed columns are Make/Model (/MaxLen 16) and Mileage (/MaxLen 7). Five-digit mileages would not fit a 16-char Make/Model column error and vice versa, so a wrong-column write shows up as garbage rather than as a plausible number.

SECTION 4 COMPLETION (map v4). digital_assets carries FIVE records against four slots - the fifth is dropped and logged. Every digital-asset cell is /MaxLen-free, so cell size proves NOTHING about which column a value landed in; that table is the one place in Section 4 where only distinct per-column values can expose a mis-assignment. Hence every one of the twenty cells is unique and names its own row and column.

Digital-asset values are deliberately NOT wallet addresses, exchange account identifiers, seed phrases or key material - not even fabricated ones. The location column holds an obviously fictional custodian name and the name column holds 'Placeholder Coin' labels. Anything shaped like a real key would be a liability in a checked-in fixture regardless of whether it resolved to anything.

life_insurance_policies is NOT a row table. The form prints three POLICY COLUMNS by five rows (17a name/address, 17b policy number, 17c owner, 17d cash value, 17e loan balance), so each record here is one printed column. Policy number and owner are distinct per column ('POL-17-COL1-TEST' / Sample Taxpayer, COL2 / Sample Spouse, COL3 / Sample Family Trust) so a column mix-up is visible at a glance rather than hiding behind repeated values.

The 17* key prefix is the printed marker, not the internal one. The Page2 widgets are named Lines16b-f / p2_t33_16c / p2_t45_15g, and the form still carries a stale 'blocks 16b through 16f' sentence from an earlier revision. The printed markers on Rev. 6-2026 read 17a-17f, and those are what the keys follow, because these become immutable HubSpot property names.

property_line_20 rows name their own printed row ('Row 20a' / 'Row 20b'). Line 20's location and lender blocks are INVERTED against the internal field names, the same way 18b/18c and 19b/19c are: row 20a takes p3_t55_19b + Lender-phone3 and row 20b takes p3_t47_19a + Lender-phone4. Distinct descriptions, lenders and phones per row are what make that inversion checkable in the read-back.

All six Section 4 totals are arithmetic on the SLOTTED rows only, and each one is a different number, so a total written into the wrong cell shows up as a wrong number rather than a plausible one: 15e = 6105 (3800+1250+640+415, the dropped fifth digital asset's 9999 excluded), 16e = 5500 (2500+1800+900+300), 17f = 17000 (the three policies' cash value minus loan balance: 10000+4000+3000), 18d = 150000 (70000+55000+25000), 19d = 18000 (6000+7000+5000), 20c = 12500 (8000+4500).

18d, 19d and 20c are the three cross-section totals whose targets correlated only to bled street-address fragments (p3_t20_17c, p3_t40_18c, p3_t56_19c). All three were confirmed against the PRINTED markers before this sample was written, not against the field names, which disagree with the print in every case.

The four 'as of' date cells (15_digital_asset_value_as_of, 16_amount_owed_as_of, 16_available_credit_as_of, and the two already present at 13/14) are /MaxLen 8 mmddyyyy column headers, not money - same size trap as the v3 pair.
